context:
Goal: accurate work landed at the fastest speed.
Problem (goal): 177 open lane PRs hold built work with no done review record, and if nothing decides their path they sit until the stale-draft pass closes them and the work is lost.
Based on (measured): the retrospective's lost-lanes audit at 09:55 CST Nov 13 found 356 of 410 open lane PRs unbatched: 179 with a done record, 59 with a record open, bad or stale, and 118 with no record; 155 of their lanes are archived.
Based on (ruling): your 09:26 CST Nov 13 call on step handin-cannot-drop makes every PR with a done record join a batch mechanically, so the 179 are already decided and this question covers only the 177.
Based on (read): stale-draft closes on all 356 are held until you pick.
Departs from: main, where the stale-draft pass closes old drafts — adds a sort of these 177 before any close, with their steps following the outcome.

options.gain: Fresh work lands soon, and old work is rebuilt on current rules instead of fixed through conflicts.
options.how: PRs under 48 h old get lane-lint and one fresh Sonnet review each, then join batches newest first. PRs 48 h or older are closed with a note, and their steps go back to ready to rebuild under today's rules.
options.label: Split by age (recommended)
options.lose: Some good old work is built twice.

options.how: Every one of the 177 gets lane-lint and one fresh Sonnet review, then joins batches, whatever its age.
options.label: Review and batch all 177
options.lose: Many reviews and batches; old PRs need conflict fixes, and some carry rules you have since changed.

options.gain: A clean queue on current rules.
options.how: Each of the 177 is closed with a note, and its step goes back to ready.
options.label: Close all 177 and rebuild
options.lose: About 177 builds are redone, including recent work that only needed a review.

short: Built lane PRs with no done review
title: What happens to 177 built lane PRs whose review record is missing, open or stale?
why: Your 09:26 CST call covers PRs with a done review: they join batches mechanically. These 177 have no done review, and no ruling of yours says whether to review them or rebuild them.
